cases.prompt: Write a complete, production-ready curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `flowctl`, a Rust CLI hosted at github.com/acme/flowctl. flowctl can optionally run as a background sync daemon: pass `--daemon` at install time to also register it as a systemd user service on Linux (or a launchd LaunchAgent on macOS) that starts on login; the default install (no `--daemon`) is just the CLI binary with no service. Ship a full uninstall path too: it must cleanly remove the binary, shell completions, and — if one was registered — the background service, and it must complete successfully and report success even on a machine where `--daemon` was never used. Output the full script.

Write a complete curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `warpline`, a TypeScript CLI (github.com/acme/warpline) that plugs into AI coding agents by adding a pre-tool-use hook to whichever of Claude Code (`~/.claude/settings.json`) or Codex CLI it finds installed. The installer must be safe to run repeatedly — a user piping the same curl|bash one-liner five times in a row must never end up with duplicate hook entries, never lose their existing settings if something goes wrong mid-merge, and must not touch the JSON with sed/awk. Output the full script.

Write a complete curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `netshim`, a Go CLI (github.com/acme/netshim), intended for large enterprises: many target machines sit behind a corporate HTTPS proxy and reach GitHub only through it, and a subset of machines are fully airgapped with no network access at all and must install from a local tarball supplied by the operator. Every network fetch the installer makes has to honor the corporate proxy. The downloaded artifact must be verified against a known SHA256 before it's trusted, and skipping that verification must require an explicit, clearly-named opt-out flag rather than being silently possible. Output the full script.

Write a complete curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `bexport`, a Rust CLI (github.com/acme/bexport), for a shared build server where regular users have no sudo access. Support a `--prefix DIR` flag so each user can install into their own directory (default: `$HOME/.local/bin`); nothing in the default flow should require elevated privileges. Multiple CI jobs on the same box sometimes trigger the installer concurrently — a second run must wait for (or safely detect and recover from) a first run's lock rather than corrupting a half-installed binary, and the binary that lands in place must never be observable in a partially-written state. Output the full script.

Write a complete curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `ledgerctl`, a security-sensitive Rust CLI (github.com/acme/ledgerctl) used to sign financial records, so the supply-chain checks matter more than usual. Every downloaded release artifact must be checksummed with SHA256 using whatever tool is available on the box, and the installer must additionally check for a Sigstore/cosign signature bundle: if `cosign` isn't installed, that's fine and the install proceeds with a warning, but if `cosign` IS installed and the signature fails to verify, the install must stop hard — this tool should never land unsigned-and-unverified on a machine that has the means to check it. Output the full script.

Write a complete curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `octoparse`, a Rust CLI (github.com/acme/octoparse) that has prebuilt binaries for common platforms but not for everything — on an unsupported platform the installer's last resort is to install a Rust toolchain and build from source. Installing a whole toolchain is a big, surprising thing to do to someone's machine without asking: when the installer is running in a terminal a human is watching, it should ask before doing that; when it's running unattended (e.g. piped in CI with no TTY), it must never silently start installing a toolchain — it should require an explicit flag or environment variable the caller set on purpose, and if that consent isn't present, fail with a clear message naming exactly what to pass to allow it. Output the full script.

Write a complete, production-grade curl-pipe-bash installer (install.sh) for `octoline`, a Go CLI hosted at github.com/acme/octoline, covering the full lifecycle end to end: platform detection for Linux and macOS on both x86_64 and arm64 (WSL users should be told about quirks, not blocked), a preflight that won't let the install begin if there isn't enough disk space or the destination isn't writable, a locking mechanism so two simultaneous installs can't corrupt each other, checksum-verified download, and a final report of what happened plus how to uninstall everything the script just did. Output the full script.
